ProblemSolved: Target-center bearing treats a finite vehicle as a point and can overstate off-axis exposure for close targets.
Purpose: Compare target-center bearing with the nearest lateral body-edge bearing while preserving the accepted Golden Run and Candidate identities.
Inputs: the source Golden Run resolved plan
paired Camera Width signals from the exact accepted U001 Frame View
the fingerprint-bound S1 distance bindings used to identify the corresponding Camera channels
MathematicalDefinition: x_t = selected Camera longitudinal distance in meters
y_t = selected Camera lateral position in meters
w_t = selected Camera target Width in meters
rank AUC compares descriptive ordering association with Radar invalidity; it is not a classifier acceptance metric
Assumptions: Camera Width is the lateral physical target width in meters
Camera LateralPosition refers to the target center in the same lateral coordinate system
Camera Distance, LateralPosition and Width selected from one Camera role describe the same target and FrameCount
the Camera and Radar sensor-origin offset is small enough for this first descriptive comparison
U001 validity, updated and age fields are authoritative
no cross-frame Width hold is permitted
Prohibitions: do not modify U001 source files or the accepted S1 Module
do not call Radar ground truth
do not infer Radar beam width from this experiment
do not approve a field-of-view threshold
do not classify every Radar dropout as geometry-related
do not hide centerline Radar-loss counterexamples such as reviewed Candidate C0010
Outputs: full-frame center and angular-footprint evidence CSV
directly comparable Radar-invalid rate tables by center and nearest-edge angle
Candidate-level footprint summaries preserving B16 identities
EvaluationPlan: verify exact paired Width identities through the accepted U001 catalog and the source S1 distance bindings
require Width to be valid, updated in the same frame, age zero and positive
compare center-angle and nearest-edge-angle descriptive association over identical eligible rows
inspect reviewed close-range Candidates C0014 and C0016 for reduced nearest-edge angle
retain reviewed C0010 as a central non-geometric comparison
promote SelectedCameraWidth into a future S1 interface only if the experiment materially improves engineering interpretation
Limitations: DBC definitions of Width and LateralPosition still require business confirmation before a physical field-of-view claim
target orientation, foreshortening, occlusion, reflector location and Radar antenna pattern are not modeled
Camera-reported Width may be an estimate rather than measured ground truth
rank AUC is sensitive to population composition and temporal dependence
video review remains mandatory for engineering conclusions
DecisionRule: B17 may justify a formal S1 SelectedCameraWidth interface change only when Width coverage is sufficient and nearest-edge geometry resolves reviewed close-range contradictions without erasing central-loss counterexamples.
